course.title: Fragrance Making
course.tagline: Blend your own perfumes and body oils, from scent notes to a bottled product.

days.title: Welcome to Fragrance Making
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Your kit is essential oils, carrier oils, perfumer's alcohol, bottles, pipettes and a scale.

video.title: How to Make Perfume Step by Step

steps: Get your tools ready: perfumer's alcohol, essential oils and glass bottles.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: A scale measures fragrance ingredients accurately.
Your kit is essential oils, carrier oils, perfumer's alcohol, bottles, pipettes and a scale. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise welcome to fragrance making on a model or a practice head. Your kit is essential oils, carrier oils, perfumer's alcohol, bottles, pipettes and a scale. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do welcome to fragrance making two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: What is the key point of today's lesson on welcome to fragrance making?
options: You should rush through the technique to save time.
A scale measures fragrance ingredients accurately.
The best result comes from skipping the preparation step.
You never need to check your work until the very end.
quiz.explain: A scale measures fragrance ingredients accurately.

quiz.q: Which tool is most essential for welcome to fragrance making?
quiz.explain: The perfumer's alcohol is the essential tool for this work.

quiz.q: What should you always do when working on welcome to fragrance making?
options: check the client for cuts before starting
patch test new blends on skin
quiz.explain: You should always patch test new blends on skin.
